title: A Body Blow? The War on Iran and U.S. Military Readiness
gist: A podcast episode note: the U.S. war against Iran is straining military readiness by consuming munitions and missile-defense interceptors, extending deployments and diverting forces from other theaters, with implications for deterrence and a China crisis.

insights.claim: The U.S. war against Iran is consuming munitions and missile defense interceptors, extending deployments and diverting forces and attention from other theaters, which is straining U.S. military readiness.
insights.speaker: Mark Cancian, Stacie Pettyjohn, Michael Eisenstadt, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: Interceptor and munitions depletion points to multi-year replenishment demand for missile-defense and munitions makers.
insights.locator: The war against Iran is putting

insights.claim: Readiness depletion from the Iran war weakens U.S. deterrence and its ability to respond to a crisis with China.
insights.speaker: Mark Cancian, Stacie Pettyjohn, Michael Eisenstadt, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: A thinner U.S. force posture in Asia is a factor in Taiwan and Indo-Pacific risk assessments.
insights.locator: The war against Iran is putting
